newsitem.title: ICELAND: Iceland to launch market maker system for crown.
newsitem.headline: Iceland to launch market maker system for crown.

text.p: Iceland's Central Bank said on Friday it would introduce a market making system for the Icelandic crown from July 8 as part of changes to lay the foundations for a continuous interbank market.
The central bank said its role in the foreign exchange market would be reduced.

The central bank's daily fixing meetings for the currency will be abandoned and the central bank will fix the official exchange rate of the crown on the basis of indicative prices quoted by other market participants between 10.45 and 11.00 a.m. each trading day.
"The central bank can also base the official exchange rate on actual trading prices made at that time if it decides to intervene in the market," the bank said in a statement.

Market makers will be asked to make binding offers and bids for at least $0.5 million. Market makers will also be obliged to quote on a current basis indicative bids and offers for that amount in U.S. dollars.

The central bank's exchange rate policy will remain unchanged and a stable rate within a set target range of plus or minus six percent remains the intermediate target of monetary policy, the central bank said.
"Larger fluctuation can though be expected in the exchange rate of the crown, both within trading days and between trading days," the bank added.
Iceland introduced an interbank foreign exchange market in 1993. The changes bring Iceland into line with many of its neighbours and major trading partners.
Simultaneously, the central bank issued new rules on foreign exchange exposure, reserve requirement and liquidity ratio.

The maximum for total foreign exchange exposure for Icelandic banks is raised from 20 percent to 30 percent of equity and from 10 to 15 percent in individual currencies except U.S. dollar, where the maximum exposure will be 20 percent of equity.
